findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_prop_probabilities · Private data: get_team_stats, get_head_to_head, get_predictions · Public sink: get_game_detail, get_odds, get_line_movement, get_player_props, get_prop_history, get_prop_movement, get_market_odds, get_game_probabilities, get_prop_probabilities, get_alt_lines · Destructive: get_market_odds, get_alt_lines.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_prop_probabilities · Private data: get_team_stats, get_head_to_head, get_predictions · Public sink: get_game_detail, get_odds, get_line_movement, get_player_props, get_prop_history, get_prop_movement, get_market_odds, get_game_probabilities, get_prop_probabilities, get_alt_lines · Destructive: get_market_odds, get_alt_lines

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "get_player_game_log" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
